source: Synthesized from CDC's 2022 'Learn the Signs Act Early' developmental-milestone update (set to 75th percentile presentation, 2, 4, 6, 9, 12, 15-month official checklists) and AAP HealthyChildren ages-and-stages guidance (1-month, 3-month, 7-month, 12-month stage pages). Each entry's source_url points at the most specific authority for that milestone. CDC 2022 reference: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/index.html
notes: age_window_low_days is the earliest age at which the milestone typically first appears for most term infants (clinical literature + AAP stage guidance). age_window_high_days is the CDC 2022 checkpoint by which 75% of children have demonstrated the skill (for CDC-listed items) or the high end of the AAP stage-page range (for items not on a CDC checklist). Past high_days and still pending is worth raising with the pediatrician — not necessarily pathologic, but the right moment for clinical input. Surface from low_days; never surface earlier. The check-in section sorts by seed_order so the most foundational items appear first.

milestones.display_name: Moves both arms and both legs
milestones.clinical_note: Symmetric, spontaneous movement of all four limbs. Asymmetry warrants pediatric attention.

milestones.display_name: Reacts to loud sounds (startle, blink, stillness)
milestones.clinical_note: Confirms intact hearing response. Universal newborn hearing screen catches most cases but daily observation matters.

milestones.display_name: Brings hands within range of eyes and mouth
milestones.clinical_note: Early body awareness. Not yet purposeful — looks like accidental discovery.

milestones.display_name: Turns head side to side while on tummy
milestones.clinical_note: Protective reflex — keeps airway clear during tummy time.

milestones.display_name: Focuses on objects 8-12 inches away
milestones.clinical_note: Natural breastfeeding distance. Newborn vision is otherwise blurry.

milestones.display_name: Looks longer at human faces than other patterns
milestones.clinical_note: Innate social orientation. Hold babies 8-12 inches from your face during alert windows.

milestones.display_name: Quiets or turns toward a familiar voice
milestones.clinical_note: Voice recognition begins before birth; postnatally it shows as orienting or settling to a parent's voice.

milestones.display_name: Watches your face when you talk
milestones.clinical_note: Baseline social orientation. Look for sustained gaze, even briefly, during alert windows.

milestones.display_name: Calms when picked up or spoken to
milestones.clinical_note: Early co-regulation. Not the same as stopping crying immediately — look for any shift in state.

milestones.display_name: Briefly lifts head during tummy time
milestones.clinical_note: Few seconds of head lift, even with bobble, counts. Builds neck strength for later head control.

milestones.display_name: First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
milestones.clinical_note: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.

milestones.display_name: Follows a moving object with eyes past midline
milestones.clinical_note: Hold a small object 8-12 inches away and slowly move side to side. Eyes should cross the body midline.

milestones.display_name: Seems happy to see you when you walk up
milestones.clinical_note: Recognition + positive affect. Often accompanied by limb-pumping excitement.

milestones.display_name: Looks at a toy for several seconds
milestones.clinical_note: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.

milestones.display_name: Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
milestones.clinical_note: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.

milestones.display_name: Holds head up while on tummy
milestones.clinical_note: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.

milestones.display_name: Hands relax open most of the time
milestones.clinical_note: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.

milestones.display_name: Smiles on his own to get your attention
milestones.clinical_note: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.

milestones.display_name: Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
milestones.clinical_note: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.

milestones.display_name: Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to keep your attention
milestones.clinical_note: Active engagement — baby is now driving the interaction, not just responding.

milestones.display_name: Turns head toward the sound of your voice
milestones.clinical_note: Localizes sound source. Worth raising with the pediatrician if absent at the 4-month visit.

milestones.display_name: Makes sounds back when you talk to him
milestones.clinical_note: Conversational turn-taking. Foundation for later vocabulary growth.

milestones.display_name: Opens mouth when she sees the breast or bottle
milestones.clinical_note: Anticipatory recognition — feeding is now associated with the sight, not just the sensation.

milestones.display_name: Looks at her hands with interest
milestones.clinical_note: Self-discovery. Often accompanied by extended fascinated staring.

milestones.display_name: Holds head steady without support when held
milestones.clinical_note: Critical safety milestone — allows for forward-facing carriers, less head-and-neck cradling.

milestones.display_name: Pushes up on elbows during tummy time
milestones.clinical_note: Tripod position. Builds toward eventual rolling.

milestones.display_name: Holds a toy when you put it in his hand
milestones.clinical_note: Voluntary grasp emerging. Soon followed by reaching.

milestones.display_name: Brings hands to mouth on purpose
milestones.clinical_note: Body awareness; precursor to self-feeding and oral exploration.

milestones.display_name: Uses arm to swing at hanging toys
milestones.clinical_note: Pre-reaching swiping — not yet visually-guided grasp.

milestones.display_name: Laughs out loud
milestones.clinical_note: Full belly laugh, not just a smile with sound. Often triggered by gentle physical play or peekaboo.

milestones.display_name: Reaches to grab a toy he wants
milestones.clinical_note: Visually-guided reaching, eye-hand coordination.

milestones.display_name: Uses voice to express joy and displeasure
milestones.clinical_note: Distinct vocalizations for different states — early affective communication.

milestones.display_name: Rolls from tummy to back
milestones.clinical_note: Usually appears first — back-to-tummy follows later. Once rolling begins, stop swaddling for sleep.

milestones.display_name: Supports whole weight on legs when held standing
milestones.clinical_note: Builds leg strength for eventual pulling-to-stand. Does not need to bear weight independently.

milestones.display_name: Rolls from back to tummy
milestones.clinical_note: Harder direction; requires more core and upper-body strength.

milestones.display_name: Reaches for objects with one hand
milestones.clinical_note: Differentiation from earlier two-handed swiping — emerging hand preference is normal but unstable until ~age 3.

milestones.display_name: Moves things from one hand to the other
milestones.clinical_note: Bilateral coordination across the midline. Often accompanied by mouthing the transferred object.

milestones.display_name: Pushes up with straight arms during tummy time
milestones.clinical_note: Full arm extension, chest off the floor. Builds toward sitting.

milestones.display_name: Leans on hands to support self when sitting
milestones.clinical_note: Tripod sit. Precedes hands-free sitting by 1-2 months.

milestones.display_name: Knows familiar people (parents vs strangers)
milestones.clinical_note: Different reaction (calming, leaning in) for parents vs strangers. Precursor to stranger anxiety.

milestones.display_name: Likes to look at himself in a mirror
milestones.clinical_note: Doesn't yet recognize as self, but visually attentive.

milestones.display_name: Takes turns making sounds with you
milestones.clinical_note: Reciprocal vocal exchange. Pause after speaking, wait for response.

milestones.display_name: Blows raspberries (sticks tongue out and blows)
milestones.clinical_note: Oral-motor practice. Often coincides with starting solids.

milestones.display_name: Makes squealing noises
milestones.clinical_note: Exploring pitch range. Can be loud — normal.

milestones.display_name: Puts things in mouth to explore them
milestones.clinical_note: Primary mode of sensory exploration. Time to audit floor-level small-object hazards.

milestones.display_name: Closes lips to show she doesn't want more food
milestones.clinical_note: Pre-verbal refusal. Important to respect — supports developing satiety cues.

milestones.display_name: Enjoys back-and-forth social play
milestones.clinical_note: Active turn-taking in physical or vocal games. Distinct from earlier passive enjoyment of stimulation.

milestones.display_name: Responds to other people's emotional expressions
milestones.clinical_note: Crying when a parent is sad, brightening when a parent laughs. Foundation of empathy.

milestones.display_name: Distinguishes emotions by tone of voice
milestones.clinical_note: Reacts differently to a stern vs warm voice with the same words.

milestones.display_name: Finds a partially hidden object
milestones.clinical_note: Beginning of object permanence — fully hidden objects come later.

milestones.display_name: Struggles to reach objects that are out of reach
milestones.clinical_note: Goal-directed behavior. Often precedes intentional rolling or scooting toward an object.

milestones.display_name: Begins to respond to the word 'no'
milestones.clinical_note: Pauses briefly when the word is said. Compliance is a much later milestone.

milestones.display_name: Shows shyness or anxiety with strangers
milestones.clinical_note: Healthy attachment signal, even when intense. Peaks 8-12 months.

milestones.display_name: Shows several facial expressions (happy, sad, angry, surprised)
milestones.clinical_note: Differentiated affect. Look for context-appropriate expressions, not just a varied repertoire.

milestones.display_name: Looks when his name is called
milestones.clinical_note: Worth raising with pediatrician if consistently absent at the 9-month visit.

milestones.display_name: Reacts when you leave (looks, reaches, or cries)
milestones.clinical_note: Beginning of separation anxiety. Different from earlier protests that are mostly about loss of stimulation.

milestones.display_name: Smiles or laughs during peekaboo
milestones.clinical_note: Anticipates the reappearance — early prediction skill, not just sustained social engagement.

milestones.display_name: Babbles long strings like 'mamamama' or 'bababababa'
milestones.clinical_note: Canonical babbling. Strong predictor of speech development.

milestones.display_name: Lifts arms when wanting to be picked up
milestones.clinical_note: Pre-verbal communicative gesture.

milestones.display_name: Looks for objects when dropped out of sight
milestones.clinical_note: Beginning of object permanence. Makes peekaboo suddenly the funniest thing in the world.

milestones.display_name: Bangs two things together
milestones.clinical_note: Cause-and-effect exploration.

milestones.display_name: Sits without support
milestones.clinical_note: Hands free for play. WHO motor study cites 3.8-9.2 mo as the typical range.

milestones.display_name: Gets to a sitting position on her own
milestones.clinical_note: Active transition into sitting from lying down. Often precedes crawling.

milestones.display_name: Uses fingers to 'rake' food toward herself
milestones.clinical_note: Pre-pincer grasp. Coincides with starting finger foods.

milestones.display_name: Crawls forward on belly (combat crawl)
milestones.clinical_note: Pulling with arms, pushing with legs, belly on the floor. Precedes hands-and-knees crawling.

milestones.display_name: Crawls on hands and knees, or scoots
milestones.clinical_note: Some babies skip crawling and go straight to cruising — that is within normal range.

milestones.display_name: Moves from sitting into a crawl or lie-down position
milestones.clinical_note: Postural transition. Predicts comfortable independent exploration.

milestones.display_name: Pulls to stand at furniture or your legs
milestones.clinical_note: Time to switch to a lower crib mattress setting if not already.

milestones.display_name: Babbles with inflection (sounds like speech)
milestones.clinical_note: Jargon. Pitch and rhythm of a sentence without recognizable words.

milestones.display_name: Explores objects by shaking, banging, throwing, dropping
milestones.clinical_note: Systematic property exploration. Repetitive drops are research, not defiance.

milestones.display_name: Lets objects go voluntarily (drops on purpose)
milestones.clinical_note: Controlled release — distinct from accidental dropping. Predecessor to throwing.

milestones.display_name: Pokes with index finger
milestones.clinical_note: Isolated finger use. Predecessor to pointing.

milestones.display_name: Picks up small bits with thumb and index finger (pincer grasp)
milestones.clinical_note: Fine motor milestone with major implications for self-feeding.

milestones.display_name: Shows specific preferences for certain people and toys
milestones.clinical_note: Stable preferences — different from the more diffuse preferences of early infancy.

milestones.display_name: Repeats sounds or gestures to get your attention
milestones.clinical_note: Intentional communication via repetition. Looks like 'showing off'.

milestones.display_name: Plays peekaboo (initiates by covering and uncovering face)
milestones.clinical_note: Active game initiation, not just smiling when you hide. Demonstrates object permanence in action.

milestones.display_name: Plays games like pat-a-cake
milestones.clinical_note: Imitative gesture game. Joint attention + motor imitation.

milestones.display_name: Waves bye-bye
milestones.clinical_note: Intentional gesture with social meaning.

milestones.display_name: Calls a parent 'mama' or 'dada' or another name
milestones.clinical_note: Specifically referring to a person, not generalized babble. First true word for many babies.

milestones.display_name: Understands 'no' (pauses or stops when you say it)
milestones.clinical_note: Receptive language. Compliance is a much later milestone.

milestones.display_name: Uses simple gestures (shaking head 'no')
milestones.clinical_note: Conventional gesture use — different from spontaneous babbling-with-motion.

milestones.display_name: Responds to simple verbal requests
milestones.clinical_note: Single-word commands ('give', 'come'). Predates two-step instructions by months.

milestones.display_name: Looks at the correct picture when you name it
milestones.clinical_note: Receptive vocabulary builds rapidly here. Best surveyed during book time.

milestones.display_name: Imitates gestures (waves, claps when you do)
milestones.clinical_note: Deferred imitation comes later; this is concurrent imitation.

milestones.display_name: Puts something in a container
milestones.clinical_note: Demonstrates planning and spatial reasoning.

milestones.display_name: Takes objects out of a container
milestones.clinical_note: Often appears before put-in. Tip-the-bucket is the favorite version.

milestones.display_name: Looks for things you hide (under a blanket)
milestones.clinical_note: Object permanence consolidated.

milestones.display_name: Cries or protests when a parent leaves the room
milestones.clinical_note: Peak separation anxiety. Healthy attachment, even when it makes drop-off hard.

milestones.display_name: Drinks from an open cup as you hold it
milestones.clinical_note: AAP recommends open-cup or weighted-straw cup over sippy cups for oral-motor development.

milestones.display_name: Extends arm or leg to help when being dressed
milestones.clinical_note: Cooperative participation in care routines — early sign of mutual social rhythm.

milestones.display_name: Walks while holding on to furniture (cruising)
milestones.clinical_note: Independent walking usually follows within 2-3 months.

milestones.display_name: Stands alone for a few seconds
milestones.clinical_note: Often follows cruising. Balance precedes locomotion.

milestones.display_name: Uses objects appropriately (cup, phone, book)
milestones.clinical_note: Functional use — picks up phone and puts it to ear, holds book the right way. Pretend play emerges from here.

milestones.display_name: Takes a few steps on her own
milestones.clinical_note: CDC checkpoint is 15 months. Wide normal range — late walking alone is not concerning if other milestones are on track.

milestones.display_name: Uses one word besides mama or dada
milestones.clinical_note: Commonly 'ball', 'dog', 'bye', or a family-specific word.

milestones.display_name: Tries to imitate words you say
milestones.clinical_note: Approximations count. 'Wa' for water is a real attempt.

milestones.display_name: Uses exclamations like 'uh-oh!'
milestones.clinical_note: Affect-laden word-like utterances. Often the earliest 'words' parents recognize.

milestones.display_name: Tries to imitate scribbling
milestones.clinical_note: Whole-arm marks, not yet wrist-driven. Crayon grip is full-fist.

milestones.display_name: Claps hands when excited
milestones.clinical_note: Spontaneous expressive gesture — not just imitation.

milestones.display_name: Shows affection (hugs, cuddles, kisses)
milestones.clinical_note: Spontaneous affectionate gestures, not just receiving them.

milestones.display_name: Shows you an object she likes
milestones.clinical_note: Joint attention with intention to share — distinct from pointing to request. Strong autism-screen marker when consistently absent.

milestones.display_name: Follows directions given with a gesture and words
milestones.clinical_note: Combined verbal + nonverbal cues. Pure-verbal compliance comes after.

milestones.display_name: Points to ask for something or to get help
milestones.clinical_note: Imperative pointing. Declarative pointing ('look at that') typically follows.

milestones.display_name: Looks at a familiar object when you name it
milestones.clinical_note: Receptive vocabulary in action — 'where's the ball?' triggers a head turn.

milestones.display_name: Copies other children while playing
milestones.clinical_note: Peer-directed imitation, not just imitation of parents.

milestones.display_name: Hugs a stuffed doll or other toy
milestones.clinical_note: Pretend nurture — early symbolic play. Often emerges with a favorite lovey.

milestones.display_name: Stacks at least two small objects (like blocks)
milestones.clinical_note: Visuomotor coordination + planning. Knocking the stack down is also part of the practice.
